enrichment.sped_program_notes: BC districts use "Inclusive Education" / "Special Education" terminology under the BC School Act and Ministry of Education Special Education Policy Framework, not U.S. IDEA. Students with special needs are designated under BC's Categories (A–Q) rather than IDEA eligibility categories. Individualized Education Plans (IEPs) do exist in BC and are legally required for designated students, so there is conceptual overlap with Journify's IEP drafting and goal-tracking features — but the regulatory vocabulary, compliance forms, and audit requirements differ substantially from U.S. norms. IEP system of record is likely a BC-specific platform (e.g., MyEdBC / MyEducation BC) rather than Frontline, SEIS, or other Journify-integrated U.S. platforms. Integration pathway is currently unknown and likely requires custom development.

email_draft.subject: Mission SD's inclusive education team, less paperwork | Journify
email_draft.body:
Your team at SD #74 supports designated students across Mission's schools, and the documentation load that comes with BC's IEP requirements is real regardless of which side of the border you're on.

With roughly 756 students on IEPs, your inclusive education staff are likely spending a significant portion of each week on plan writing, progress notes, and parent communication rather than direct student support. Journify is purpose-built to reduce that burden across the whole support team, including case managers, paraprofessionals, and related-service providers. Most teams report getting back more than four hours per day once IEP drafting and goal tracking move through an AI-assisted workflow.

Worth a 20-minute conversation to see whether Journify maps to how BC IEPs are structured at your district?
